title: Fallback replay — command log and breadcrumbs
content:
Notes to self: quick replay checklist and command history for the multi-region fallback incident on 2026-02-11. Intended as a reproducible scratchpad to run later in staging and to hand off to oncall for follow-up.

Summary / what happened
- Around 2026-02-11T21:06Z we saw a spike of route_ejections + regional fallbacks originating from EU-west (az-eu-3).
- Clients observed elevated latency and ~2.7% 5xxs for about 18 minutes; smart-routing triggered fallback to compatible model variant in us-central for some traffic.
- Automatic rollback to primary region was slow; suspect policy hysteresis + bad kvcache priming.

Observations gathered (metrics + quick reads)
- Route ejection metric: route_policy.eject_count[route=chat-text,region=eu-west] increased from 0 to 106 over 6m.
- Error class in traces: "handshake_timeout" + "kv_cache_miss" mixed with failed tcp handshakes.
- Token lat p50 jumped 30ms -> 220ms for routed requests to fallback target.
- Tracing showed request ids that crossed regional boundary had missing kv_cache headers (x-kv-prefix absent).

Immediate commands I ran (copy/paste friendly)
# grab recent traces for region slice (3x sources)
kubectl -n prod logs deploy/route-proxy --since=25m | rg "region=eu-west" -B3 -A4 | sed -n '1,500p' > /tmp/eu-west-traces-20260211.log

# sample telemetry query (metrics backend)
curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/query?metric=route_policy.eject_count&from=2026-02-11T20:50Z&to=2026-02-11T21:30Z&tag=route:chat-text" | jq . > /tmp/eject-count.json

# fetch routing table at time of incident (config-db)
redis-cli -h conf-db.prod.internal HGETALL "routes:chat-text:2026-02-11T21:00Z" > /tmp/route-config-snapshot.txt

# check last rollout for model variant used as fallback
gh pr view 842 --json title,body,commits > /tmp/pr-842-summary.txt

# repro request to emulate region failure by forcing route header (staging)
curl -v -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west" -H "X-Force-Route: chat-text" -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY" \
  "https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":10}' --write-out "\\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code}\\n" --connect-timeout 6 --max-time 10 > /tmp/repro-response-1.txt 2>&1

Observed snippet (from repro-response-1.txt):
> * Connection timed out after 6001 milliseconds
> HTTP_CODE:000
> curl: (28) Operation timed out after 6002 milliseconds with 0 out of 0 bytes received

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Prefix/KV cache warming mismatch: some routed requests lost the x-kv-prefix header and hit cold model instances in fallback region -> cold start latency cascades and then triggers ejection policy.
2) Network egress flakiness between eu-west and internal infra (TCP handshake timeouts) causing route-proxy to mark backend unhealthy and initiate fallback.
3) Fallback policy threshold combined with slow retries (3 retries x 5s) exaggerated the outage window.
4) Load/queueing: sudden burst caused queue growth; autoscaler in dedicated pools didn't scale fast enough for fallback targets.

Error snippets pulled from logs
[route-proxy] 2026-02-11T21:07:12Z ERROR route-eject route=chat-text region=eu-west reason=handshake_timeout details="tcp handshake failed to 10.12.45.9:443 after 5000ms" trace_id=tr-0a1b2c
[kv-sync] 2026-02-11T21:07:14Z WARN kv-cache miss prefix=absent route=chat-text instance=fallback-us-3
[router] 2026-02-11T21:09:01Z INFO fallback-invoked route=chat-text target_variant=chat-small-v2 reason=policy_eject

Replay / repro plan (staging, controlled)
- Goal: reproduce route_eject behavior deterministically and capture full packet traces + spans.
- Steps:
  1) deploy a config with short eject thresholds in staging (eject_error_rate>1% over 30s) so we can trigger without broad impact. -> config name: test-eject-short
  2) instrument a small load generator to send 200 qps with X-Client-Region: eu-west header for 10 minutes.
  3) simultaneously introduce intermittent packet loss to fallback target (tc qdisc netem 100ms delay 10% loss) on staging fallback nodes.
  4) run the same curl repro above to observe curl timeout behavior.

Commands to set up simulated network flakiness (staging nodes)
# SSH into fallback node (staging-fb-3)
ssh core@staging-fb-3
sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem delay 100ms loss 10% 25%
# when done:
sudo tc qdisc del dev eth0 root netem

Load generator (minimal)
# quick golang wrk-style loop (run from bastion)
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west" -H "X-Force-Route: chat-text" -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY" \
    "https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" &
  sleep 0.005
done

Trace capture tips
- Start tcpdump on both sides to capture SYN retransmits and timestamps: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/fb-syns.pcap 'tcp port 443 and (tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-syn != 0)'
- Increase sampling rate in tracing (temporarily) for route-proxy: setenv TRACE_SAMPLING=0.8 in deployment config and rollout.

Quick bash 'replay' script prototype (staging)
cat > /tmp/replay-failover.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
STAGING_KEY=REDACTED
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  curl -s -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west" -H "X-Force-Route: chat-text" -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY" \
    "https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"ping","max_tokens":6}' --max-time 8 -o /tmp/p.$i.json &
  sleep 0.1
done
wait
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/replay-failover.sh

Notes about traces and correlation
- Capture request ids (x-request-id) from route-proxy logs and align with trace ids. Some traces from the incident had missing kv-pref tags which correlate with the kv-cache miss warnings.
- Pay attention to rollout metadata: if fallback target was a different model family (eg chat-small-v2 vs chat-base) we will see tokenization differences and potentially token-level latency variance.

What to check post-replay (artifacts to gather)
- pcap files from both sides /tmp/fb-syns.pcap
- route-proxy logs with trace ids (time window)
- redis conf-db snapshot used for routing keys
- metrics snapshot: route_policy.eject_count, token_latency_p50/p95, instance_cpu, queue_length
- sample payloads and responses to check for missing x-kv-prefix header

Short-term mitigations to propose (if reproduced)
- Reduce eject hysteresis or increase sensitivity window to prevent mass-ejection cascades (only as a temporary experiment).
- Add aggressive KV prefetching for recently-failed routes to avoid cold-start hits on fallback targets.
- Add a temporary network health proxy to detect cross-region TCP anomalies and mark them for manual review instead of automatic full-eject.

Open questions / TODOs
- Did the routing config use 'regional-preference=soft' or 'hard'? need to confirm from conf-db snapshot.
- Which commit introduced the fallback variant change 2026-02-10? correlate with GH PR 842.
- Should we add a "grace window" for kv-pref absence before ejecting? (hypothesis: 30s)

Hand-off checklist (for next oncall)
- Run replay script in staging, collect pcaps and logs, upload to shared debugging bucket: gs://redwood-debug/fallback-replays/2026-02-11/
- Attach route-proxy logs + trace ids to JIRA CON-4281 and ping Priya for model-family context.
- If reproduced, propose rollout of prefetched-kv experiment to prod-canary group.

End of scratchpad. Will refine after staging replay.

-- Aisha
